name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q01 - Propagation of mechanical waves across different elastic media

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Transverse mechanical waves can propagate through solids as well as along the free surface of liquids.

Statement II: Longitudinal mechanical waves can propagate through all elastic media including solids, liquids, and gases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding transverse waves
Transverse mechanical waves involve particle oscillations perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, producing shearing deformation. These waves require a non-zero shear modulus (modulus of rigidity) to provide the necessary restoring force. Solids possess a definite shear modulus, and liquid surfaces can sustain transverse ripple disturbances due to surface tension and gravity. Therefore, transverse waves can travel through solids and on the surface of liquids. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding longitudinal waves
Longitudinal mechanical waves involve oscillations along the direction of propagation, consisting of compressions and rarefactions that cause volumetric strain. The restoring force is governed by the bulk modulus of elasticity. Because solids, liquids, and gases all possess non-zero bulk moduli and resist compression, longitudinal waves can propagate through all three states of matter. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Both evaluated propositions are physically sound and factually accurate across all described media.

Final Answer
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q02 - Physical transport of matter and particle oscillations in waves

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a progressive mechanical wave, the medium as a whole moves bodily from the source to the receiver along with the wave disturbance.

Statement II: In a transverse progressive wave, the constituent particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding medium transport
A mechanical wave is the propagation of a localized disturbance through an elastic medium. While energy and momentum are transferred across space, the constituents of the medium only execute simple harmonic oscillations about their respective mean equilibrium positions without any net bodily displacement of matter. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding transverse particle oscillation
By definition, a transverse wave is one in which the elements of the medium oscillate in a direction perpendicular (normal) to the direction of wave propagation, not parallel to it. Oscillations parallel to wave propagation characterize longitudinal waves. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Neither of the two propositions correctly describes the kinematic behavior of progressive waves or the direction of particle motion in transverse waves.

Final Answer
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q03 - Laplace correction and adiabatic bulk modulus of gases

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Laplace corrected Newton's formula by establishing that the compressions and rarefactions in a sound wave occur adiabatically rather than isothermally.

Statement II: The adiabatic bulk modulus of an ideal gas is equal to its pressure \(P\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding Laplace correction
Newton originally assumed that sound propagation is an isothermal process, leading to the theoretical speed \(v = \sqrt{P/\rho}\), which was about 15% lower than the experimental value in air. Laplace recognized that compressions and rarefactions take place so rapidly that heat exchange with the surrounding air is negligible, making the process adiabatic. This modification successfully reconciled the formula with experimental observations. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding adiabatic bulk modulus
For an adiabatic process in an ideal gas, \(P V^\gamma = \text{constant}\). Differentiating this relation yields \(V^\gamma \Delta P + \gamma P V^{\gamma - 1} \Delta V = 0\), which gives the adiabatic bulk modulus \(B_{\text{ad}} = -\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V / V} = \gamma P\). The isothermal bulk modulus is \(B_{\text{iso}} = P\). Because \(\gamma > 1\) for all real gases, the adiabatic bulk modulus is \(\gamma P\), not \(P\). Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
The thermodynamic classification introduced by Laplace is valid, but the adiabatic elasticity of an ideal gas is scaled by the ratio of specific heats \(\gamma\).

Final Answer
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q04 - Dependence of sound speed on pressure and temperature

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At a constant temperature, the speed of sound in an ideal gas increases proportionally with the square root of its pressure.

Statement II: The speed of sound in an ideal gas is directly proportional to the square root of its absolute temperature in kelvin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding pressure dependence
The Laplace formula for the speed of sound in an ideal gas is \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}\). According to Boyle's law at constant temperature, pressure is directly proportional to density (\(P \propto \rho\)), which means the ratio \(\frac{P}{\rho}\) remains strictly constant regardless of pressure changes. Therefore, sound velocity in an ideal gas is completely independent of pressure at constant temperature. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding temperature dependence
Substituting the ideal gas law \(\frac{P}{\rho} = \frac{R T}{M}\) into the velocity equation gives \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\). For a given gas, the parameters \(\gamma\), \(R\), and \(M\) are constants, which establishes that the speed of sound is directly proportional to \(\sqrt{T}\), where \(T\) is the absolute temperature in kelvin. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Varying the pressure isothermally leaves sound speed unchanged, whereas temperature changes alter the thermal velocity and thus the sound speed according to a square root relation.

Final Answer
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q05 - Principle of superposition and interference of harmonic waves

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When two identical harmonic waves with equal amplitude \(a\) interfere with a phase difference of \(\pi\) radians, the resultant displacement is zero everywhere at all times.

Statement II: The amplitude of the resultant wave formed by the superposition of two identical waves differing only by a phase constant \(\phi\) is \(2a \cos(\phi / 2)\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding destructive interference
According to the principle of superposition, the resultant wave of two co-propagating harmonic waves of identical amplitude \(a\) and wavelength is given by \(y(x, t) = 2a \cos(\phi/2) \sin(kx - \omega t + \phi/2)\). When the phase difference is \(\phi = \pi\text{ rad}\), the cosine factor becomes \(\cos(\pi/2) = 0\). Consequently, the net displacement vanishes identically throughout space and time, producing complete destructive interference. Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding resultant amplitude
Using the trigonometric identity \(\sin A + \sin B = 2 \sin\left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \cos\left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right)\), the addition of \(y_1 = a \sin(kx - \omega t)\) and \(y_2 = a \sin(kx - \omega t + \phi)\) directly yields the amplitude term \(A(\phi) = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Both mathematical expressions derived from the principle of wave superposition correctly describe the resultant wave amplitude and the condition for complete destructive interference.

Final Answer
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q06 - Harmonics in open versus closed organ pipes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An organ pipe open at both ends produces only odd harmonics of its fundamental resonant frequency.

Statement II: An organ pipe closed at one end produces all integral harmonics (both even and odd) of its fundamental resonant frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding open organ pipes
An open organ pipe has antinodes at both of its open ends. The permissible resonant modes require an integral number of half-wavelengths to fit the length \(L\), meaning \(L = \frac{n\lambda}{2}\). This gives resonant frequencies \(\nu_n = n \left(\frac{v}{2L}\right)\) where \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4, \dots\). Therefore, an open pipe generates all integral harmonics (both even and odd), not only odd harmonics. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding closed organ pipes
An organ pipe closed at one end forms a displacement node at the closed boundary and an antinode at the open boundary. The allowed lengths correspond to an odd number of quarter-wavelengths, \(L = (2n - 1)\frac{\lambda}{4}\), yielding resonant frequencies \(\nu_n = (2n - 1)\left(\frac{v}{4L}\right)\) for \(n = 1, 2, 3, \dots\). Thus, a closed pipe produces only odd harmonics, and even harmonics are entirely absent. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
The statements have transposed the acoustic properties of the two types of pipes: open columns support all harmonics, whereas columns closed at one end support exclusively odd harmonics.

Final Answer
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q07 - Phase change and boundary displacement during wave reflection

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a transverse travelling wave pulse on a flexible string reflects from a rigid fixed boundary, it suffers a phase reversal of \(\pi\) radians.

Statement II: When a transverse travelling wave pulse reflects from a completely free boundary, the boundary point experiences a net maximum displacement of zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding rigid boundary reflection
At a rigid boundary, the string is held fixed so that the net displacement must remain zero at all times (\(y = 0\)). By Newton's third law, the support applies an equal and opposite reactionary force on the arriving pulse, launching an inverted pulse travelling in the reverse direction. This inverted reflection corresponds to an abrupt phase change of \(\pi\text{ rad}\) (or \(180^\circ\)). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding free boundary reflection
At a completely free boundary (such as a massless ring sliding without friction on a vertical post), the boundary can support no transverse force, meaning the spatial slope \(\frac{\partial y}{\partial x}\) must be zero. The incident and reflected waves arrive in phase (phase shift of \(0\text{ rad}\)). By superposition, the displacements add constructively, resulting in a maximum displacement at the boundary equal to twice the pulse amplitude (\(2a\)), rather than zero. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
Reflection at a fixed end creates destructive interference with a phase change of \(\pi\) to maintain zero displacement, whereas reflection at a free end creates constructive reinforcement doubling the peak displacement.

Final Answer
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q08 - Beat frequency relation and auditory persistence limit

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When two sound waves of slightly different frequencies \( u_1\) and \( u_2\) interfere, the frequency of the resulting intensity beats is \( rac{ u_1 + u_2}{2}\).

Statement II: For human ears to distinctly resolve and count the periodic waxing and waning of sound intensity in beats, the difference between the two frequencies should typically not exceed 10 Hz.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the proposition regarding beat frequency
When two sinusoidal sound waves of frequencies \( u_1\) and \( u_2\) interfere, the mathematical envelope modulating the acoustic amplitude varies at angular frequency \( rac{|\omega_1 - \omega_2|}{2}\). Because intensity is proportional to the square of amplitude, the intensity reaches a maximum twice per modulation cycle, yielding an intensity beat frequency \( u_{ ext{beat}} = | u_1 - u_2|\). The term \( rac{ u_1 + u_2}{2}\) represents the average pitch or carrier frequency of the combined note, not the frequency of the beats. Hence, this proposition is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the proposition regarding the human auditory threshold for beats
The persistence of hearing for the human ear is approximately \(0.1 ext{ s}\). If the time interval between successive intensity peaks is shorter than \(0.1 ext{ s}\) (corresponding to a beat frequency greater than approximately \(10 ext{ Hz}\)), the distinct waxing and waning sensations merge into a single continuous unpleasant sensation called dissonance. Thus, distinct beats can be individually heard and counted only when \(| u_1 - u_2| \le 10 ext{ Hz}\). Hence, this proposition is correct.

Step 3: Synthesis and Conclusion
The beat frequency is the absolute frequency difference rather than the average, and the human ear can resolve distinct beats only within the limit set by auditory persistence.

Final Answer
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
